product: Largest private-sector power producer and largest US nuclear operator, with 55 GW across nuclear, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, wind and solar, plus competitive retail supply to about 2.5 million customer accounts nationwide.
demand: Data-center and AI load plus corporate sustainability targets drive demand; the company signed an additional 920 MW of 15-20 year nuclear PPAs in Q2 2026, including 176 MW with Walmart enabling a 30 MW Dresden expansion, and added a 15-year Toyota renewable deal in September 2026.
pricing_power: Scale plus long-dated contracts support pricing power: MarketBeat describes the nuclear fleet as roughly twice the nearest competitor, and Constellation is signing 15-20 year PPAs with investment-grade customers rather than selling only merchant power.
competition: Vistra, Talen, NRG, NextEra and other independent power producers compete for data-center and retail load, while rival nuclear and gas developers compete for interconnection rights, nuclear fuel and skilled labor.
team: Joe Dominguez is chairman, president and chief executive officer, adding the chairman role effective Aug 4 2026; Shane Smith is chief financial officer; Roger Crandall, MassMutual chairman and CEO, joined the board Aug 5 2026; Dan Verbanac leads retail and solutions.
market_strategy: Integrate Calpine into a dispatchable coast-to-coast fleet, lock long-term PPAs with investment-grade corporates, restart Crane in 2027, extend nuclear licenses, add bolt-ons like RISEC, and return capital via 5 billion dollars of buybacks through 2027.
bull: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS $2.55 beat $2.29 estimate and FY guidance was raised to $11.50-12.50; 920 MW of 15-20 year investment-grade PPAs signed, including Walmart 176 MW, plus a 15-year Toyota REC deal on Sep 21 2026.
bear: Q2 revenue $7.50B missed $7.73B, GAAP EPS fell to $1.42 from $2.67, nuclear output dropped to 44,160 GWh, diluted shares rose to 360M from 314M, and six of seven 90-day analyst actions cut targets (net -6 raises).
falsifier: Q3 2026 earnings (est. 2026-11-09) showing FY adjusted EPS guidance below $11.50 or another GAAP EPS decline with nuclear output down again.
web_what_changed: Last 90 days: Aug 6 2026 Q2 results, adjusted EPS 2.55 dollars vs 2.29 dollars estimate, FY guidance raised to 11.50-12.50 dollars; Aug 4 dividend of 0.4265 dollars; Aug 5 Dominguez added chairman role, Roger Crandall joined board; Sep 10 agreement to buy 609 MW RISEC gas plant from Shell for 715 million dollars; Sep 21 Toyota 15-year REC deal; 860 million dollar Brazos Valley sale to LS Power.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No Constellation disclosure dated Sep 24 or Sep 25 2026 was located; the latest primary item read is the Sep 21 2026 Toyota renewable agreement, and the IR events page lists no new upcoming event. MarketBeat close for Sep 24 2026 was 261.62 dollars.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Demand-led and mix-led, not volume. Q2 2026 revenue rose 23 percent year over year to 7.50 billion dollars, which the company attributes to adding Calpine plus favorable market and portfolio conditions; 920 MW of new 15-20 year PPAs were signed, including Walmart at 176 MW. Nuclear output fell to 44,160 GWh from 45,170 GWh on outages.
web_suppliers: Not found on primary sources read. No Constellation-named supplier set was located on its IR site or the Q2 release. Aggregator evidence shows nuclear fuel and enrichment are the constrained link, with Rosatom holding roughly 44 percent of global enrichment capacity and Centrus plus DOE building HALEU capacity; gas turbine OEMs also gate new gas capacity.
web_customers: Concentrated in very large corporates but with a broad retail tail. Constellation reports about 2.5 million customer accounts and roughly 80 percent of the Fortune 100. Q2 2026 disclosed 920 MW of 15-20 year PPAs with investment-grade customers, including Walmart 176 MW for Dresden; Microsoft and Meta were named earlier (aggregator).
web_who_loses: Rival merchant power producers chasing the same data-center and retail load, notably Vistra, Talen, NRG and gas peakers, lose share and pricing leverage. Retail suppliers lose accounts to Constellation bundling generation with supply. Independent nuclear developers lose scarce interconnection rights, fuel and skilled outage labor to a larger incumbent.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q2 2026 revenue of 7.50 billion dollars missed the 7.73 billion dollar estimate and GAAP EPS fell to 1.42 dollars from 2.67 dollars, with nuclear output down year over year. The stock fell 13 percent over six sessions from Sep 9 to Sep 18 2026, closing at 254.71 dollars on Calpine seller share overhang and rising yields; diluted shares rose to 360 million from 314 million; most recent analyst actions cut targets.
web_if_management_right: Crane restarts in 2027 after the FERC capacity interconnection rights waiver and NRC fuel license approval; the 920 MW of new PPAs begin 2029 through 2032; RISEC closes and is immediately accretive above the 10 percent unlevered return threshold; FY 2026 adjusted EPS lands in the 11.50-12.50 dollar range and the 5 billion dollar buyback completes by end 2027.
web_if_management_wrong: Calpine integration, purchase-accounting amortization and share dilution keep GAAP earnings below adjusted earnings; power prices or data-center demand stall; the Calpine seller overhang keeps pressuring the stock; and RISEC spending plus buybacks strain the balance sheet while the adjusted-to-GAAP gap stays wide.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Named in primary reads: Ferrovial Energy Milano Solar project, contracted for more than 115 MW, Toyota buying RECs, and LS Power buying Brazos Valley. Also uranium and enrichment suppliers, gas turbine and grid equipment makers, nuclear services and outage labor, and Texas and New England gas pipeline infrastructure.
